from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the scene layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Problem: The Noisy Channel", 
            [
                "Digital data travels through noisy, imperfect environments.",
                "Interference can flip a bit from zero to one.",
                "We must fix errors without re-sending the message."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Represent Alice and Bob
        alice_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE)
        alice_label = Text("Alice (Cat)", font_size=18).next_to(alice_circle, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        alice = VGroup(alice_circle, alice_label)
        self.place_in_area(alice, "A1", "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bob_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GREEN)
        bob_label = Text("Bob (Dog)", font_size=18).next_to(bob_circle, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        bob = VGroup(bob_circle, bob_label)
        self.place_in_area(bob, "E5", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Message setup
        bit_vals = ["1", "0", "1", "1"]
        bits = VGroup(*[Text(b, font_size=32, color=WHITE) for b in bit_vals]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        msg_box = SurroundingRectangle(bits, buff=0.2, color=WHITE)
        message = VGroup(bits, msg_box)
        
        self.place_at_grid(message, "B2", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(alice), Create(bob))
        self.play(Create(message))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Noise cloud
        cloud_circles = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.4, fill_opacity=1, color=YELLOW_A),
            Circle(radius=0.5, fill_opacity=1, color=YELLOW_A).shift(RIGHT*0.4),
            Circle(radius=0.4, fill_opacity=1, color=YELLOW_A).shift(LEFT*0.4),
            Circle(radius=0.3, fill_opacity=1, color=YELLOW_A).shift(UP*0.3)
        )
        cloud_label = Text("NOISE", font_size=16, color=BLACK).move_to(cloud_circles.get_center())
        cloud = VGroup(cloud_circles, cloud_label)
        self.place_in_area(cloud, "C3", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Animation: Move message towards Bob
        # Stop mid-way for noise interference
        self.play(message.animate.move_to(self.grid["C3"]), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Flash noise cloud
        self.play(FadeIn(cloud))
        self.play(cloud.animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.2, rate_func=there_and_back)
        
        # Flip bit 3 (index 2) from 1 to 0
        flipped_bit = Text("0", font_size=32, color=RED).move_to(bits[2])
        self.play(
            bits[2].animate.set_color(RED),
            Transform(bits[2], flipped_bit)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Continue move to Bob
        self.play(message.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"]), FadeOut(cloud), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Red question mark appears above Bob
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(question_mark, "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(question_mark))
        
        # Display Goal text
        goal_text = Text("Goal: Fix the error without re-sending.", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(goal_text, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(goal_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'A parity bit ensures the count of ones is even.',
            'One bit flip makes the total count odd.',
            'Simple parity detects errors but cannot locate them.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Simple Parity Bit", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_GREEN = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_RED = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display '110' (#FFFFFF) and append even parity bit '0' (#00FF00).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_GREEN)
        
        data_bits = VGroup(
            Text("1", color=COLOR_WHITE),
            Text("1", color=COLOR_WHITE),
            Text("0", color=COLOR_WHITE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(data_bits, "B2", "B4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        parity_bit = Text("0", color=COLOR_GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(parity_bit, "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        data_label = Text("Data Bits", font_size=18, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(data_label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        parity_label = Text("Even Parity", font_size=18, color=COLOR_GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(parity_label, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(data_bits), FadeIn(data_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(parity_bit), FadeIn(parity_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flip the last bit to '1' (#FF0000); show total 1s is 3 (Odd).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_RED)
        
        error_bit = Text("1", color=COLOR_RED)
        self.place_at_grid(error_bit, "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Note: We replace the parity bit with an error bit to simulate corruption
        count_msg = Text("Total 1s = 3 (Odd!)", color=COLOR_RED, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(count_msg, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Transform(parity_bit, error_bit))
        self.play(Write(count_msg))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display 'Error Detected' (#FF0000) near Bob; location unknown.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_RED)
        
        error_alert = Text("Error Detected", color=COLOR_RED, font_size=30)
        self.place_in_area(error_alert, "D2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        bob_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.6, width=1.2, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        bob_text = Text("Bob", color=COLOR_WHITE, font_size=20)
        bob_vgroup = VGroup(bob_box, bob_text)
        self.place_at_grid(bob_vgroup, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        unknown_label = Text("But which bit is wrong?", color=COLOR_RED, font_size=20)
        self.place_in_area(unknown_label, "F2", "F5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bob_vgroup))
        self.play(FadeIn(error_alert))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(unknown_label))
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'Hamming used overlapping circles to check data bits.',
            'Place four data bits in the overlapping regions.',
            'Add three parity bits to the outer circles.',
            'Every data bit is covered by multiple parity checks.',
            'This redundancy allows us to pinpoint errors.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hamming Logic: Overlapping Circles", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for the circles
        p1_color = "#FF5733" # Reddish
        p2_color = "#33FF57" # Greenish
        p4_color = "#3357FF" # Blueish

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Draw three overlapping circles
        c1 = Circle(radius=2.3, color=p1_color, stroke_width=4, fill_opacity=0.2)
        c2 = Circle(radius=2.3, color=p2_color, stroke_width=4, fill_opacity=0.2)
        c4 = Circle(radius=2.3, color=p4_color, stroke_width=4, fill_opacity=0.2)

        self.place_in_area(c1, "B3", "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(c2, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(c4, "D5")

        self.play(Create(c1), Create(c2), Create(c4), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Data bits: D3, D5, D6, D7 (Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX requirement)
        d3 = Text("D3", font_size=34, color=WHITE)
        d5 = Text("D5", font_size=34, color=WHITE)
        d6 = Text("D6", font_size=34, color=WHITE)
        d7 = Text("D7", font_size=34, color=WHITE)

        # Place data bits in intersections
        self.place_in_area(d3, "C2", "C3", scale_factor=1.0) # P1 & P2
        self.place_in_area(d5, "C4", "C5", scale_factor=1.0) # P1 & P4
        self.place_in_area(d6, "E3", "E4", scale_factor=1.0) # P2 & P4
        self.place_in_area(d7, "C3", "D4", scale_factor=1.0) # All (Center)

        self.play(Write(VGroup(d3, d5, d6, d7)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Parity bits: P1, P2, P4 (Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX requirement)
        p1_lbl = Text("P1", font_size=34, color=p1_color)
        p2_lbl = Text("P2", font_size=34, color=p2_color)
        p4_lbl = Text("P4", font_size=34, color=p4_color)

        # Place parity bits in outer petals
        self.place_in_area(p1_lbl, "A3", "A4", scale_factor=1.0) # Top
        self.place_in_area(p2_lbl, "E1", "E2", scale_factor=1.0) # Left
        self.place_in_area(p4_lbl, "E5", "E6", scale_factor=1.0) # Right

        self.play(Write(VGroup(p1_lbl, p2_lbl, p4_lbl)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        # Highlight Circle P1: P1, D3, D5, D7
        self.play(c1.animate.set_stroke(width=10, opacity=1), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(p1_lbl, d3, d5, d7), color=p1_color))
        self.play(c1.animate.set_stroke(width=4, opacity=1), run_time=0.5)

        # Highlight Circle P2: P2, D3, D6, D7
        self.play(c2.animate.set_stroke(width=10, opacity=1), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(p2_lbl, d3, d6, d7), color=p2_color))
        self.play(c2.animate.set_stroke(width=4, opacity=1), run_time=0.5)

        # Highlight Circle P4: P4, D5, D6, D7
        self.play(c4.animate.set_stroke(width=10, opacity=1), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(p4_lbl, d5, d6, d7), color=p4_color))
        self.play(c4.animate.set_stroke(width=4, opacity=1), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Emphasize redundancy (bit 7)
        self.play(
            c1.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.4),
            c2.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.4),
            c4.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.4),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(Indicate(d7, scale_factor=2.0, color=YELLOW), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            'Parity bits occupy positions that are powers of two.',
            'Remaining positions hold the actual message data bits.',
            'Each parity bit monitors a specific set of positions.',
            'Binary addresses define which parity bits cover which data.',
            'This creates a unique coordinate for every bit.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Strategic Placement (Powers of 2)", lecture_lines)

        # Pre-create bit slots and labels
        # Positions: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7
        # We'll use Row B for 1-4 and Row C for 5-7
        slots = VGroup()
        indices = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7"]
        grid_pos = ["B1", "B2", "B3", "B4", "C1", "C2", "C3"]
        
        bit_boxes = {}
        bit_labels = {}
        
        for idx, g_pos in zip(indices, grid_pos):
            box = Square(side_length=0.8, color=GRAY, stroke_width=2)
            self.place_at_grid(box, g_pos)
            
            label = Text(idx, font_size=20, color=WHITE)
            label.next_to(box, UP, buff=0.1)
            
            bit_boxes[idx] = box
            bit_labels[idx] = label
            slots.add(box, label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Parity bits occupy positions that are powers of two.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        self.play(FadeIn(slots))
        
        # Highlight powers of 2 (1, 2, 4) in Gold
        parity_indices = ["1", "2", "4"]
        p_label_objs = VGroup()
        for idx in parity_indices:
            p_text = Text(f"P{idx}", font_size=24, color=GOLD)
            self.place_at_grid(p_text, grid_pos[indices.index(idx)], scale_factor=1.0)
            p_label_objs.add(p_text)
            self.play(
                bit_boxes[idx].animate.set_color(GOLD).set_stroke(width=4),
                FadeIn(p_text),
                run_time=0.5
            )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Remaining positions hold the actual message data bits.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE_B)
        )
        
        data_indices = ["3", "5", "6", "7"]
        d_label_objs = VGroup()
        for idx in data_indices:
            d_text = Text(f"D{idx}", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
            self.place_at_grid(d_text, grid_pos[indices.index(idx)], scale_factor=1.0)
            d_label_objs.add(d_text)
            self.play(FadeIn(d_text), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Each parity bit monitors a specific set of positions.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN_B)
        )
        
        # Highlight logic: P1 checks 1, 3, 5, 7
        highlight_p1 = VGroup(*[bit_boxes[i] for i in ["1", "3", "5", "7"]])
        rect_p1 = SurroundingRectangle(highlight_p1, color=GOLD, buff=0.1)
        p1_info = Text("P1: Checks 1, 3, 5, 7", font_size=20, color=GOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(p1_info, "E1", scale_factor=0.8)
        p1_info.shift(RIGHT*1.5)
        
        self.play(Create(rect_p1), FadeIn(p1_info))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(rect_p1), FadeOut(p1_info))

        # Highlight logic: P2 checks 2, 3, 6, 7
        highlight_p2 = VGroup(*[bit_boxes[i] for i in ["2", "3", "6", "7"]])
        rect_p2 = SurroundingRectangle(highlight_p2, color=GOLD, buff=0.1)
        p2_info = Text("P2: Checks 2, 3, 6, 7", font_size=20, color=GOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(p2_info, "E1", scale_factor=0.8)
        p2_info.shift(RIGHT*1.5)

        self.play(Create(rect_p2), FadeIn(p2_info))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(rect_p2), FadeOut(p2_info))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Binary addresses define which parity bits cover which data.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(PINK)
        )
        
        # Show binary address for 3: 011
        bin_addr = Text("3 = 011 (binary)", font_size=24, color=PINK)
        self.place_at_grid(bin_addr, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        bin_addr.shift(RIGHT*1.0)

outline.topic: Error Correction Codes: The Magic of Hamming Codes

sections.title: The Problem: The Noisy Channel
sections.content: Introduce the concept of data corruption during transmission. Explain that in the digital world, a 0 can flip to a 1 due to heat, interference, or distance. Establish the goal: not just knowing an error happened, but fixing it without re-sending the data.
sections.example: Alice (a cat) sends a binary 'fish' code (1011) to Bob (a dog) through a rainy cloud. The rain flips one bit, and Bob receives (1001). Bob needs to realize the error and fix it himself.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Simple Parity Bit
sections.content: Explain the concept of 'Even Parity'. A single bit added to the end of a message to make the total number of 1s even. Highlight its limitation: it detects an odd number of errors but cannot tell which bit is wrong.
sections.example: Message: 110. Total 1s = 2 (Even). Parity bit = 0. New message: 1100. If it arrives as 1101, Bob knows it's wrong (3 is odd), but he doesn't know if the error is in the data or the parity.

sections.title: The Hamming Logic: Overlapping Circles
sections.content: Introduce Richard Hamming's breakthrough. Instead of one parity bit for the whole message, use multiple parity bits that cover overlapping subsets of the data. Use a Venn Diagram visualization (3 overlapping circles) to represent Hamming(7,4).
sections.example: Visualize 3 circles (A, B, C). Place 4 data bits in the intersections and 3 parity bits in the outer 'petals'. Each parity bit is responsible for maintaining 'evenness' within its specific circle.

sections.title: Strategic Placement (Powers of 2)
sections.content: Explain the mathematical rule for bit positioning. Parity bits are placed at positions that are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8...). Every data bit's position is then uniquely represented by the sum of these powers (e.g., Position 3 = 1 + 2).
sections.example: In a 7-bit sequence: P1, P2, D3, P4, D5, D6, D7. P1 checks all positions with a '1' in their binary representation's last digit (1, 3, 5, 7). P2 checks positions with a '1' in the second-to-last digit (2, 3, 6, 7).

sections.title: The 'Aha!' Moment: Identifying the Culprit
sections.content: Show how to find the erroneous bit using 'Syndrome Calculation'. When a bit flips, multiple parity checks will fail. The sum of the positions of the failing parity bits points exactly to the index of the corrupted bit.
sections.example: If Parity Circle 1 and Parity Circle 2 both show an error, but Circle 4 is fine: 1 + 2 = 3. Position 3 is the liar! Bob flips the bit at Position 3 back to its original state.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Conclude with where this is used today. Highlight ECC (Error Correction Code) RAM, spacecraft communication (Voyager), and QR codes. Emphasize that Hamming Code is the foundation of modern reliable digital storage.
sections.example: A high-end server uses ECC RAM. Even if a cosmic ray flips a bit in the middle of a complex calculation, the Hamming-based logic fixes it instantly, preventing a system crash.
